title: Brane Cosmology
description: Our universe is a membrane floating in the Bulk. The Brane Shifter can take you there.

puzzle.goal: Our universe is a 4D membrane at one end of a fifth dimension y running from −πr to πr, and the 5D metric shrinks the 4D part by a warp factor e^(−2k|y|). The 5D gravity strength M³ is turned into the 4D one by integrating the action over y: the volume element contributes e^(−4k|y|) and the 4D curvature term e^(+2k|y|). Write the effective 4D Planck mass squared.
puzzle.name: Randall–Sundrum warped extra dimension (effective 4D gravity scale)
puzzle.form: M ^ 3 * int ( - π * r , π * r , exp ( - 4 * k * abs ( y ) ) * exp ( 2 * k * abs ( y ) ) , y )
puzzle.ask: The integral gives (M³/k)(1 − e^(−2kπr)) ≈ M³/k, so M and k are of order the Planck scale, yet a mass m0 on the far brane at |y| = πr appears to us reduced by the warp factor e^(−kπr). Find the apparent mass (GeV) of m0 = 1.22e19 GeV for k = 1 and r = @{r} (in units of 1/k).

vars.m0: mass parameter on the hidden brane

puzzle.method: Reduce the 5D action ∫d⁴x dy √−G M³ R over y: √−G carries four powers of the warp factor e^(−k|y|), the inverse metric in R removes two. Integrate the leftover exponential over both halves of the orbifold.
